L01.text: If you jumped into a hole straight through the Earth, you'd come out the other side in thirty-eight minutes.

L02.text: The deepest hole we've ever actually dug is twelve kilometers.

L03.text: That's about a tenth of one percent of the way through.

L04.text: So let's cheat. One tunnel, pole to pole, with all the air pumped out. Jump!

L05.text: Down through the crust, then almost three thousand kilometers of hot rock.

L06.text: Weirdly, gravity gets stronger as you fall, all the way to the core.

L07.text: Thirteen minutes in, you plunge into an ocean of liquid iron.

L08.text: Near the center it's about six thousand degrees. As hot as the surface of the Sun.

L09.text: At the center, you're doing over twenty-eight thousand kilometers an hour, and you weigh nothing at all.

L10.text: Now gravity pulls you back. You slow down, and down, and down.

L11.text: Thirty-eight minutes after you jumped, you stop, right at the far side.

L12.text: Grab the edge. Miss it, and you fall all the way back. Forever.

L13.text: Unless you leave the air in. Then drag holds you to about two hundred kilometers an hour.

L14.text: After more than a day of falling, you'd end up floating at the center of the Earth. Weightless. Stuck.
